div.head: Northu 54
div.ab: Gif friðgeard sy on hwæs lande abuton stan oððe treow oððe wille oððe swilces ænigge fleard, þonne gilde se ðe hit worhte lahsliht, healf Criste healf landrican.
Gif friðgeard sy on hwæs lande abuton stan oððe treow oððe wille oððe swilces ænigge fleard, þonne gilde se ðe hit worhte lahsliht: healf Criste healf landrican.

Wenn auf jemandes Landgute eine Friedensstätte [Zuflucht magischer Weihe] ist um einen Stein oder Baum oder Quell herum oder irgend derlei [abergläubische] Thorheit, dann zahle, wer es hergerichtet hat, Rechtsbruchbusse, halb Christo [dem Bischofe], halb dem Immunitätsherrn.

If on anyone's land there is a sanctuary [a refuge of magical consecration] around a stone or tree or spring, or any such [superstitious] folly, then let him who made it pay lahslit, half to Christ [the bishop], half to the lord with jurisdiction.
If there is on anyone's land a sanctuary round a stone or a tree or a well or any such nonsense, he who made it is then to pay lahslit, half to Christ and half to the lord of the estate.
If there is a hallowed space on anyone's property near a stone or a tree or a well or any silliness of this sort, then the one who made it is to pay lahslit: half to Christ, half to the local lord.

note.seg: Nicht bloss ‘Einfriedigung’ (Rieger, Sweet), sondern ‘sanctuary’ (Thorpe, Earle Agsa. liter. 67), wie die Wörter friðhus, -socn, -splot, -stol, -stow ‘Asyl’ (s. d. Gl 1) übersetzen
Not merely ‘enclosure’ (Rieger, Sweet), but ‘sanctuary’ (Thorpe, Earle Agsa. liter. 67), as the words friðhus, -socn, -splot, -stol, -stow translate ‘asylum’ (see that word in Gl 1)

Nicht ‘Ding der Art’ Schmid; vielmehr ‘Trugbild, Wahn’. Vgl. Gl Zauber 1. a. Dieselbe Zusammenstellung der magischen Zaubers teilhaften well, stan, treow bei den Predigern ed. Assmann Bibl. Agsä. Prosa III 143 und dem II Cn 5, 1¹ zitierten

Not ‘Ding der Art’ Schmid; rather ‘phantom, delusion’. Cf. Gl Zauber 1. a. The same grouping of well, stan, treow, as sharing in magic sorcery, is found in the homilists ed. Assmann Bibl. Agsä. Prosa III 143 and in the one quoted at II Cn 5, 1¹
